plain: Dishonest use of power for gain, such as taking bribes

webster.text: The act of corrupting, or state of being corrupt or putrid; the destruction of the natural form of bodies, by the separation of the component parts, or by disorganization, in the process of putrefaction.

more.text: Putrescence; a foul state occasioned by putrefaction.
Depravity; wickedness; perversion or deterioration of moral principles; loss of purity or integrity.
Debasement; taint; or tendency to a worse state.

example.quote: To have required the unanimous ratification of the thirteen States, would have subjected the essential interests of the whole to the caprice or corruption of a single member.
